subject: Intermittent hairpin routing causing amplified latency and 5xx spike — exec attention
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@starkretail.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: stark-retail-sre@starkretail.com
Date: 2028-06-17T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: [URGENT] sudden latency & 5xx surge (10:50-11:10 PT)

Neha —

We started seeing a sharp spike in tail latency and 5xxs from 10:50–11:10 PT this morning. Dashboard shows ~6x median token latency and a 12% 5xx rate on our inference route (model: rwd-13B). Attached is a short sample of aggregated 5xx logs and a couple of example request IDs.

What we see so far:
- Error window: 10:50–11:10 PT
- Primary failure: backend 502/504 and timeouts at proxy layer
- Customers impacted: web checkout + internal batch scorer jobs

We opened this to our cloud provider (ticket attached) but needed to escalate to Redwood since traces show some calls looping before reaching your edge. Can someone confirm if there were routing changes, peering flaps, or firewall rule rollouts around that time?

Attachments: aggregate-5xx-log-sample.csv

Thanks — we need a high-level ETA and whether you can pin us to a preferred VPC peer while this is investigated.

Elaine Park
Director SRE, Stark Retail
elaine.park@starkretail.com
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elaine Park <elaine.park@starkretail.com>
Date: 2028-06-17T08:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [URGENT] sudden latency & 5xx surge (10:50-11:10 PT)

Thanks for the heads up, Elaine — I’m on it. Looping in Marissa (edge infra) and Ben (customer success / escalation lead).

Immediate asks:
- Marissa: can you pull the path traces + proxy session stats for the 10:45–11:15 PT window and look for asymmetric hops or retransmits?
- Ben: can you coordinate a short exec note and confirm whether Stark has an open procurement/contract hold that would block temporary route pinning?

If we confirm hairpinning or fallback to transit peers, we should consider a short-term route pin (preferred peer) and a conntrack/session threshold increase at the proxy to absorb the burst. I’m also happy to bring this into an exec sync if Ben thinks appropriate.

I’ve attached the Stark logs they sent.

— Neha
Neha Kapoor
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elaine Park <elaine.park@starkretail.com>
Date: 2028-06-17T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [URGENT] sudden latency & 5xx surge (10:50-11:10 PT)

Preliminary findings from path-trace and proxy logs (10:40–11:20 PT):

Summary:
- Several request flows show asymmetric hairpin routing where traffic from our US-west edge fell back to a transit peer in us-central, then back to the edge cluster. That created ~120–260ms extra RTT for affected requests.
- Proxy session table spikes at the same time; our proxy nodes reported conntrack/connlimit hits for short intervals which aligned with bursty retries. The proxy returned 502 when upstream selection timed out.
- No config rollouts recorded in the edge fleet in that window — however, a route Withdrawal event from partner-peer-7 at 10:47 PT was followed by a route announcement at 10:51 PT that prefers transit via partner-3. That explains the transient fallback.

Logs & artifacts attached: path-trace-mtr.txt (sample traces), proxy-session-stats-10-11.csv

Suggested immediate mitigations (unsafe for long-term but OK for incident window):
1) Pin Stark Retail’s prefix to our core-direct peer (peer-2) for 30 minutes to avoid hairpin fallback.
2) Increase proxy conntrack limits and socket backlog on the three affected nodes for the next 2 hours.
3) Throttle a small percentage of retry traffic at the edge to reduce amplification while we clear the session table.

I will continue deeper analysis (BGP decision logs + partner telemetry) and surface root cause; initial hypothesis is partner-peer flapping + our route preference logic triggering suboptimal path selection.

Marissa
Senior Edge Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Elaine Park <elaine.park@starkretail.com>
Date: 2028-06-17T09:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [URGENT] sudden latency & 5xx surge (10:50-11:10 PT)

Thanks Marissa — this aligns with what the Stark team observed.

Immediate plan (operational, require quick approvals):
- Action A (10:40 PT): Apply route pin for Stark prefixes to peer-2 in us-west, TTL 30 minutes — reduces extra RTT. (ops runbook available: RB-EDGE-15)
- Action B (10:55 PT): Bump proxy conntrack and backlog params on nodes edge-uw1-{01,02,03} for 2 hours; monitor session churn.
- Action C (11:05 PT): If 5xxs persist, temporarily divert low-priority batch scoring traffic to a cold cluster to relieve pressure.

Risks: brief BGP churn when pinning, possible transient increased CPU on proxies while conntrack rebalances. Recommended to schedule a 15-min post-mortem with Stark SRE.

Requesting exec ack for temporary route pin and the short config changes. Also asking for discretionary credit discussion with Stark — we should be prepared to offer a goodwill credit if they were materially impacted.

Ben Carter
Customer Escalations Manager, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@starkretail.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-06-17T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [URGENT] sudden latency & 5xx surge (10:50-11:10 PT)

Ben / Neha — thank you for the quick analysis. We approve the temporary route pin and the proxy backlog increase. Please confirm ETA for pining and expected recovery window.

Also, our finance team will open a credit request depending on measured downtime/impact. Please include a short exec note we can share internally at Stark (one pager with cause, mitigation, and next steps).

Elaine
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Elaine Park <elaine.park@starkretail.com>
Date: 2028-06-17T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Exec summary: Stark Retail hairpin-induced latency + 5xx spike (10:50–11:10 PT)

Vivek / Jonas — short summary and ask for quick approvals.

What happened:
- 10:50–11:10 PT: Stark Retail experienced elevated token latency (median ~6x) and 12% 5xx on inference traffic.
- Root cause (prelim): transient hairpin routing after partner-peer-7 withdrawal; traffic temporarily selected a transit peer path resulting in additional RTT and proxy session amplification.

Actions taken (completed):
- 09:05–09:10 PT (ops times are local): pinned Stark prefixes to preferred peer-2 (30 min), increased conntrack/backlog on three affected proxies, and throttled small portion of retry traffic. (See attached artifacts: path-trace-mtr.txt, aggregate-5xx-log-sample.csv)

Current status:
- Error rate back to baseline as of ~11:20 PT; customer reports service restored for both web and batch. Full post-incident validation underway.

Asks:
1) Approve discretionary goodwill credit discussion with Stark — they request a short one-pager they can share with finance. Recommend starting with a 10% usage credit for the impacted window, pending post-mortem.
2) Approve a partner BGP policy review (ops + partner eng) to avoid similar hairpin decision loops — low-risk scheduled work.

I will schedule a 30-min post-mortem within 48 hours and will include partner BGP decision logs and proxy telemetry.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
